display_title: Vergunning windpark IJmuiden Ver Gamma-B – Windenergie op zee
organization_or_parent_framework: Ministerie van Klimaat en Groene Groei
executive_summary: Tender, run by RVO for the Ministry of Climate and Green Growth, for the permit to build and operate an offshore wind farm of about 1 GW (up to 1.15 GW installed) on plot Gamma-B of the IJmuiden Ver wind energy area, about 61 km off the Dutch coast, with an optional operating subsidy. Wind farm developers and energy companies submit one application each, either in a zero-subsidy auction (highest one-off bid wins) or in the subsidy procedure (lowest tender amount wins), with a maximum tender amount of EUR 0.116 per kWh and a subsidy ceiling of EUR 4.698 billion paid over 15 years on actual production. Applications are open from 26 November 2026 to 10 December 2026, 17:00; the permit is expected in the first quarter of 2027 and the wind farm, which connects to TenneT's 2 GW offshore platform shared with Gamma-A, is expected in operation in 2032.
status_rationale: The tender awards the permit and a 15-year operating subsidy for building and operating a 1 GW offshore wind farm on plot Gamma-B (Regeling subsidie- en vergunningverlening kavel Gamma-B, Staatscourant 2026, 21303, articles 2, 10 to 15). It touches TenneT's field directly: the wind farm connects to TenneT's 2 GW HVDC platform shared with Gamma-A, close to the project files 2GW Program, Onshore and Offshore Grid Investment Plans 2026 and Grid Optimisation Plan (over-planting of 1.15 GW on a 1 GW export cable). Only the wind farm developer can receive the permit and subsidy, but the rules give TenneT a defined unfunded role as offshore transmission system operator: the applicant must agree TenneT's connection conditions within 12 months, and TenneT and the permit holder draw up a joint connection and test plan and test the wind farm with TenneT's grid connection system (article 3(3) and 8(5); explanatory notes § 5.3; RVO Q&A, Ontwikkelkader questions 4 to 6). The category is manufacturer-led with TenneT as unfunded system integrator and test-environment provider, because TenneT integrates the developer's wind farm into its own offshore grid and tests it there.
